S5I5 is a VECTOR DISPLACEMENT PUZZLE. Each level has pieces (gdgcpukdrl diamonds), markers (zylvdxoiuq dots), targets (cpdhnkdobh diamonds), and bars (agujdcrunq structural elements). Clicking a piece zone applies a displacement vector (+3 or -3) to a marker along one axis. The bars track marker position and constrain movement range. WIN = all markers reach their target positions. The color 6 dot and color 1 diagonal arm are visual representations derived from marker positions. Each click costs 1 step from a budget (okmxyzxpez.current_steps). Game state is fully determined by marker positions on their bars.

L1 has 2 pieces controlling 2 independent markers. Vertical piece pdzhitfvow: upper half = marker y-3, lower half = marker y+3. Horizontal piece bnbtbmhoct: left half = marker x-3, right half = marker x+3. Vertical marker starts at y=33, target at y=51 (need 6 downs). Horizontal marker starts at x=30, target at x=51 (need 7 rights). Minimum = 13 clicks. BFS confirmed.

KEY SOLVER INSIGHT: This is solvable analytically, not BFS. Each click action is a vector (dx, dy) applied to marker position. Find non-negative integer coefficients for click-vectors that sum to (target - start). This is integer linear programming / coin-change in 2D. When markers are independent (L1), it decomposes to per-axis problems. When multiple pieces affect the same marker (L2+), need to solve the coupled system. L2 has 4 pieces, 1 marker, 8 actions but only right-half clicks work (left-half = no-op when marker at bar minimum).

CRITICAL: Click displacement vectors are NOT constant. Each piece is associated with a specific bar, and the marker can only move within that bar's range. When the marker reaches a bar boundary, further clicks on that piece are no-ops. Different pieces can push the marker past other pieces' boundaries because they use different bars. This means: (1) analytical/abstract BFS with constant vectors is WRONG, (2) deepcopy BFS or engine-based simulation is needed, (3) the full pixel scan for click discovery is still valid per-level (done once from initial state), but some clicks become no-ops as marker approaches bar boundaries.
